recipes.name: Frog Eye Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package acini di pepe pasta
1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Combine pineapple juice, sugar, eggs, flour, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a saucepan. Stir and cook over medium heat until thickened.
Remove from heat; stir in lemon juice. Let cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil; add oil and remaining 2 teaspoons salt. Add pasta and cook until al dente, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Combine cooked pasta, cooled egg mixture, mandarin oranges, pineapple tidbits, crushed pineapple, and whipped topping in a large bowl; mix well. Refrigerate until chilled, 8 hours to overnight.
Before serving, add marshmallows and coconut; toss and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Frog Eye Salad
raw_recipe.description: Frog eye salad is a chilled sweet dessert made with small pasta, pineapple, Mandarin oranges, coconut, and marshmallows combined in a creamy pineapple dressing.

video.description: In this video, we turn back the clock to make a popular, retro pasta salad. This dessert salad is a combination of cooked acini di pepe pasta, pineapple juice, fruit, coconut, and marshmallows. Refrigerate overnight to set up and enjoy the next day. The recipe serves a lot, making it ideal choice for large family gatherings and potlucks.

review.reviewBody: I've made Frog Eye Salad for 20 years and I always get requests for this recipe. It's always fun to see someone else's version. I would not put coconut in anything, but that's me. Might I make a suggestion. I always do this in two steps. Make the pasta and the egg mixture first. Put it together and refrigerate it overnight. In the meantime dump all your fruits together in a bowl and put them in the fridge as well. The next day, just before serving, dump your fruit in and stir, and then add your cool whip. Keeps everything firm without melting down. I have also always used the colored minature marshmallows, it just gives the salad a more fruity flavor.

This is a wonderful recipe. However it is very addictive. Children like it as long as you use a different name and omit the coconut. The only change I make is, I boil the pasta in pineapple juice, this helps with the blandness of the pasta.

I've always considered Cool Whip disgusting and never used it in anything and always avoid it but since my husband loves it, I made this for him and to my surprise, I actually love it and find myself making it often. I find that it has a much better texture if you make sure that the pasta, fruit and egg mixture are VERY cold before adding the whipped topping. I usually put the bowl of it in the freezer for half an hour to chill it before adding the CW. I also don't thaw the CW. Makes a great difference. I also find that it tastes better with a little less than the full cup of coconut. Don't let a dislike of non dairy topping prevent you from trying this.

I have made this recipe numerous times (minus the coconut). I use a 12oz. carton of "lite" whipped topping, and also use the drained juice from the pineapple to avoid having to buy it. This recipe does make a lot so I usually cut it in half, although it is so yummy that a whole batch would get eaten in no time!

This recipe has all the pieces of being a great summer fruit salad... I marinated the pasta in the cooked mixture overnight because I made part of a day in advance, so the pasta swelled even more so! I also added blueberries, grapes and sliced bananas(just before serving). If you can find them, use the pastel colored marshmallows for added color. What a success!
Excellent dessert. I added cherries to the top and served twenty people.
I made this for my husband and daughters' and they loved it!! I just added cherries to it!!! Was delicious!!!

It seems weird to have pasta with fruit/sugar but it's good. I've made it before as the recipe states, but this time I left out the coconut and also used instant vanilla pudding (5.1 oz box)mixed with the juice from the pineapple and oranges, instead of the first 7 ingredients. It tastes just as good if not better and is a lot quicker! I only used one large can of crushed pineapple and 2 (11oz) cans of oranges and it was enough. My young kids love this salad-hubby too.

We used to make this for Christmas dinner and for big potlucks, but haven’t had it in six years since mom was diagnosed with celiac disease and had to go gluten free. I found GF acini di pepe online recently and we’re making it for Christmas dinner again. It comes in an 8.8 oz package, so we’re making a half batch, especially since it’s just for three people. I agree with everyone who said to make the pasta and egg mixture, mix and chill overnight. I can usually put the bowl in the garage overnight to chill (in Missouri), but it’s 56° today. I chill the fruit in the fridge, too. Mix everything together the day of. No coconut now, it’s a little chewy. No cherries as it turns it all pink. Plain marshmallows. My cousin made it once with fruit cocktail, that’s a big NO.

I love this salad!! In an effort to lighten it up i drained the juice from the pineapple and added a splash orange juice and combined it with 1 cup splenda, I completely left the eggs out, I achieved the same excellent results!! I also did it in 2 steps, the next morning i added fat free cool whip, only a handful of marshmellows, and about 1/2 cup coconut...achieved great taste, the family loves it!!!

Much easier recipe for this. One and 1/2 cups cooked Asini di Pepi, 1 16 oz or so can crushed pineapple with juice, 15 oz can Mandarin oranges-drained, 1 pkg instant vanilla pudding and one container cool-whip. And, yes, be careful with the pasta as it makes a lot. No need for all those other ingredients and cooking and eggs!
One of my family's favorites. My husbands grandmother used to tell the grandkids that she hunt frogs all day just so she could make this salad. Hahaha!!!
It was so bland no one ate it, very disappointing

My mom used to make this for reunions because it makes so much but it is sooooo good! Mom has dementia now and is in a home, so now I only have memories of this fun salad...we don't have reunions anymore and I can't (and shouldn't) eat the entire salad by myself, lol.
Love it. My family has been making it for years.
Instead of pasta I used pearl tapioca which is the same size Israeli Couscous. I also have made it with colored mini marshmellows
I like it like it is

Other than using JMKLEIN’s suggestion re overnight refrigeration prior to blending, and using pearl couscous instead of acini di pepe to resemble frog eyes; I followed the original recipe. It turned out amazingly wonderful and delicious!
